encounters.cc: Intermittent abdominal pain, chronic diarrhea, and 15-pound weight loss over 6 months

lines: Intermittent abdominal pain, chronic diarrhea, and 15-pound weight loss over 6 months
He presents to the clinic with a 6-month history of intermittent abdominal pain, chronic diarrhea, and a weight loss of 15 pounds.
He mentions that the diarrhea is bulky, greasy, and foul-smelling.
He also complains of joint pain that migrates between his knees, wrists, and shoulders, without any noticeable swelling or redness.
He has a past medical history of hypertension and type 2 diabetes mellitus.
- Ibuprofen 400 mg PO PRN for joint pain
Afebrile, with a blood pressure of 130/85 mmHg
Biopsy of the small intestine shows periodic acid-Schiff (PAS) positive macrophages in the lamina propria.

encounters.cc: Progressive exertional chest pain over the past 3 months

lines: Progressive exertional chest pain over the past 3 months
The patient with coronary artery disease and Whipple disease presents four months after his Gastroenterology encounter, reporting a 3-month history of progressive exertional chest pain.
He describes the pain as a pressure-like sensation in the center of his chest that occurs with walking up hills and resolves with rest.
His current medications include metformin, lisinopril, and atorvastatin.
- Ibuprofen 400 mg PO PRN for joint pain
His blood pressure is 138/86 mmHg, and his pulse is 78 beats per minute.
He is referred for a coronary angiography, which reveals a 70% stenosis in the left anterior descending artery.
An exercise stress test shows ST-segment depression in the anterior leads at a high level of exertion.
The patient is hesitant about undergoing revascularization and asks about the possibility of managing his condition with medications alone.
You recall a recent study that compared medical therapy alone to percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) plus medical therapy in patients with stable coronary artery disease.
The study concluded that there was no significant difference in the primary outcome of death, myocardial infarction, or hospitalization for unstable angina.
However, you are concerned about the possibility of a type II error due to the small sample size of the study.

encounters.cc: Follow-up appointment for persistent angina despite medical therapy

lines: Follow-up appointment for persistent angina despite medical therapy

Returning for follow-up of chest pain assessed in May 2020, the patient with coronary artery disease and Whipple disease reports compliance with his medication regimen, which includes metformin, lisinopril, and atorvastatin.
However, he has been experiencing persistent angina despite maximal tolerated doses of metoprolol.
His current symptoms limit his ability to perform moderate physical activity.
- Stable Angina Pectoris due to Coronary Artery Disease (diagnosed 2020-05-15)
He takes metformin, lisinopril, and atorvastatin; metoprolol.
- Ibuprofen 400 mg PO PRN for joint pain
Blood pressure is 132/84 mmHg, heart rate is 78 bpm
An electrocardiogram shows no new changes since his MI
The physician believes that ranolazine is appropriate for this patient due to his refractory angina and lack of other contraindications
His cardiologist recommends adding ranolazine to his regimen, but his insurance plan has denied coverage for this medication

encounters.cc: Severe pain and swelling over right knee for 2 days

lines: Severe pain and swelling over right knee for 2 days
The patient, currently managed for Whipple disease and coronary artery disease, returns for evaluation of his known crystal-induced arthropathy.
He reports that the pain worsens with movement and is associated with redness and warmth over the affected area.
He denies any recent trauma or insect bites.
He has a history of similar, less severe episodes over the past year, which resolved with NSAIDs.
- Stable Angina Pectoris due to Coronary Artery Disease (diagnosed 2020-05-15)
His medical history is significant for hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and type 2 diabetes mellitus.
- Ibuprofen 400 mg PO PRN for joint pain
On physical examination, there is a swollen, erythematous area over the prepatellar region of the right knee.
The area is tender to palpation and there is limited range of motion due to pain.
Aspiration of the bursa yields a yellowish fluid with white flecks.
- White blood cell count (WBC) in bursal fluid: 18,000 cells/µL with 90% polymorphonuclear cells
Radiographs of the right knee show punched-out erosions with overhanging edges of cortical bone.

encounters.cc: Sudden onset palpitations, chest discomfort, dizziness, and shortness of breath

lines: Sudden onset palpitations, chest discomfort, dizziness, and shortness of breath

This patient with coronary artery disease (with prior cardiology follow-up for angina) and Whipple disease describes the palpitations as sudden in onset, associated with dizziness and shortness of breath.
His chest discomfort is substernal, pressure-like, and does not radiate.
He denies any previous cardiac history.
- Stable Angina Pectoris due to Coronary Artery Disease (diagnosed 2020-05-15)
- Ibuprofen 400 mg PO PRN for joint pain
On examination, his blood pressure is 85/50 mmHg, heart rate is 180 beats per minute, respiratory rate is 22 breaths per minute, and oxygen saturation is 92% on room air
His jugular venous pressure is elevated, and lung auscultation reveals bibasilar crackles.
The ECG shows a wide complex tachycardia without discernible P waves.
Intravenous access and oxygen supplementation have been initiated.

encounters.cc: Sudden-onset shortness of breath and chest discomfort while walking

lines: Sudden-onset shortness of breath and chest discomfort while walking
The patient is a 59-year-old male with coronary artery disease and 2022 wide-complex tachycardia presenting acutely.
He reports his breathing became difficult while walking to the grocery store and has worsened rapidly over the past hour.
He now feels lightheaded and cannot lie flat without gasping for air.
- Stable Angina Pectoris due to Coronary Artery Disease (diagnosed 2020-05-15)
He has a history of hypertension and coronary artery disease but no known valvular disease.
- Ibuprofen 400 mg PO PRN for joint pain
He does not smoke and drinks alcohol socially.
His blood pressure is 98/60 mm Hg, heart rate is 112/min, and respiratory rate is 28/min.
On examination, he is diaphoretic and appears anxious.
Jugular venous distension is noted to the angle of the mandible while upright.
Cardiac auscultation reveals a new, soft, blowing holosystolic murmur best heard at the apex and radiating to the axilla.
Bibasilar crackles are present on lung auscultation.
Chest x-ray reveals bilateral pulmonary infiltrates with an enlarged left atrium.
ECG shows sinus tachycardia with no ST-segment elevations or depressions.
He is placed on supplemental oxygen, and furosemide is administered.
A Swan-Ganz catheter is inserted for hemodynamic monitoring.

encounters.cc: Sudden onset severe headache and left-sided weakness

lines: Sudden onset severe headache and left-sided weakness
This 60-year-old male with CAD, HTN, and prior ED visits for cardiac events presents with headache.
He reports the headache is severe, throbbing, and localized to the right side.
His wife notes he has been increasingly confused over the past hour.
- Stable Angina Pectoris due to Coronary Artery Disease (diagnosed 2020-05-15)
His medications include metformin, lisinopril, and atorvastatin.
- Ibuprofen 400 mg PO PRN for joint pain
His blood pressure is 190/110 mmHg, heart rate is 88 beats per minute, and he is afebrile
Neurological examination reveals decreased strength in the left lower extremity, with preserved strength in the left upper extremity.
There is no facial asymmetry, and his pupils are equal and reactive to light.
A non-contrast head CT scan shows a right-sided subdural hematoma with midline shift.

encounters.cc: Progressive weakness and confusion over 2 days following syncope

lines: Progressive weakness and confusion over 2 days following syncope
This 61-year-old male with Whipple disease and CAD presents with progressive weakness and confusion.
His wife reports that he had an episode of severe chest pain and "passed out" at home 3 days ago but refused to seek medical attention at that time.
- Stable Angina Pectoris due to Coronary Artery Disease (diagnosed 2020-05-15)
- Acute right-sided subdural hematoma with subfalcine herniation (diagnosed 2024-07-15)
- Ibuprofen 400 mg PO PRN for joint pain
Afebrile, blood pressure is 90/60 mmHg, heart rate is 110 beats per minute
His skin is jaundiced, and his abdomen is soft with mild right upper quadrant tenderness without rebound or guarding.
- Serum creatinine: 1.9 mg/dL (elevated from baseline of 1.2 mg/dL)
An electrocardiogram shows nonspecific ST and T wave changes.
